bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing OEM relationship with Hero MotoCorp described as strong, with consistent quality and reliability delivered across four manufacturing plants
- Customer diversification: OEM relationships expanded from two to four, including a long-term supply contract with Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India
- Product diversification via 68%-held subsidiary Indutch Composites Technology Private Limited in wind energy and advanced composites
- Stated focus on productivity, manufacturing and labour efficiency, quality systems and cost competitiveness
- SAP-based ERP enforcing automated controls and approval workflows, with risk-based internal audit by an independent firm of Chartered Accountants reviewed quarterly by the Audit Committee
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity / raw-material price volatility — Explicitly listed by management as shaping the operating environment and repeated in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ materially; the Company is a metal-forming auto-component maker, so input cost swings hit directly.
- Supply chain disruption — Named in both the Risk and Concerns section and the cautionary statement; the Company's stated mitigation is a structured risk management framework focused on cost optimization, operational efficiency, liquidity management and supply chain resilience.
- Geopolitical developments and trade policy shifts — Flagged by management as an environmental factor; the cautionary statement repeats economic and geopolitical conditions as a source of material variance.
- Inflation and macro demand shifts — Inflation is named in Risk and Concerns and 'demand shifts' in the cautionary statement; the whole FY26 narrative is built on a consumption recovery that management itself frames as needing to persist.
- Foreign exchange fluctuation — Listed in both Risk and Concerns and the cautionary statement, notwithstanding that foreign exchange earnings for FY 2025-26 are reported as nil ('-') against Rs 43.69 lakhs in FY 2024-25 and foreign exchange outgo as nil in both years.
- Evolving regulations, policy changes and shifting customer preferences — Named in Risk and Concerns; the cautionary statement adds regulatory or policy changes as a factor. For an auto-component supplier this covers emission/vehicle regulation and OEM platform choices.
- Competitive intensity — Named in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause results to differ materially.
- Customer concentration in a small set of OEMs — Structural concentration evident from the Company's own disclosure rather than labelled as a risk: OEM relationships have only just expanded from two to four (Hero MotoCorp, Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles), so revenue depends on a handful of platforms and the Sanand investment is explicitly tied to one customer, Tata Motors.
- Treasury / mark-to-market exposure on mutual fund investments — Management states that despite improved operating profits, profit before tax fell versus FY25 because of a mark-to-market loss on mutual fund investments, and cites the same mark-to-market valuation impact against Return on Investment and Net Profit margin - i.e. reported earnings carry non-operating market risk.

business.body: The Company manufactures automotive components - mufflers, fuel tanks, body-in-white (BIW), cradles and swing arms - supplied to vehicle OEMs from four manufacturing plants. Its customer base has expanded from two to four OEM relationships, anchored by a long-standing partnership with Hero MotoCorp, a long-term supply contract with Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India and deeper engagement with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. Through its subsidiary Indutch Composites Technology Private Limited it also participates in the wind energy and advanced composites segments, which the Company describes as supporting its product diversification strategy.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Target a step-up in both top-line and bottom-line performance over the coming years.
- Broaden the customer base beyond the historic Hero MotoCorp relationship - OEM relationships expanded from two to four, with a long-term supply contract secured with Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India and deeper engagement with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.
- Build a diversified engineering business spanning Automotive, Electronics, Aerospace and Defense.
- Sustain continued focus on productivity, manufacturing and labour efficiency, quality systems and cost competitiveness.
- Use the subsidiary Indutch Composites Technology Private Limited (wind energy and advanced composites) to support product diversification.
- Invest in the Sanand facility to serve growing Tata Motors business.
- Structured risk management framework focused on cost optimization, operational efficiency, liquidity management and supply chain resilience to sustain long-term growth.
- Human-resource priorities: build a future-ready workforce through leadership development, internal mobility, succession planning and skills-based training, supported by a digital, analytics-led HR ecosystem.
- The Board has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, published on the Company's website (munjalauto.com/finance/key-policies), and states that dividend recommendations are made on the parameters laid down in that Policy and paid out of the profits for the year. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended, and the 41st AGM notice proposes for declaration, a final dividend of 50% i.e. Re 1 per equity share of face value Rs 2 each. Governance oversight of capital deployment sits with the Board, which periodically reviews strategy, the annual business plan, business performance of the Company and its subsidiaries, technology and innovation, quality, customer centricity, capital expenditure budgets, risk management and safety and environment matters; the Managing Director apprises the Board quarterly on the overall performance of the Company including the performance of the subsidiaries. Board composition as on March 31, 2026: 7 Directors, of whom 4 (57.14%) are Independent and 2 are Women Directors (one Executive, one Independent); the Board met five times during FY 2025-26 (24-04-2025, 28-05-2025, 13-08-2025, 13-11-2025, 12-02-2026), a formal annual evaluation of the Board, its Committees, the Chairman and individual Directors was carried out, and the Chairman & Managing Director and CFO furnished the Regulation 17(8) compliance certificate. No commentary on buyback, debt reduction or credit rating appears in the routed text.
- Stated commitment to sustainable business practices with energy conservation described as one of the strong pillars of preserving natural resources.
- Programs for improving energy, efficiency and energy productivity across all operations, with optimal utilisation of power, fuel and oil and ongoing measures to improve power factor and other consumption in the core manufacturing processes.
- Rainwater harvesting and reduce-usage / reuse / recycle of water.
- Domestic sewage treatment and recycling facilities designed into all units, with the stated aim of becoming zero water discharge.
- Creating awareness and promoting sustainability amongst stakeholders.
- Human-capital commitment: a workplace built on trust, inclusion, capability building and shared growth, with leadership development, internal mobility, succession planning and skills-based training and a digital, analytics-led HR ecosystem.
- Compliance framework covers the Environment (Protection) Act 1986, the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974 and the Hazardous Wastes (Management and Handling and Transboundary Movement) Rules 1989 (stated in the secretarial audit of the material subsidiary Indutch Composites Technology Private Limited).
- No BRSR section, no quantified ESG target (emissions, energy, water, renewable share, diversity ratio) and no ESG timeline appear anywhere in the routed text - the ESG disclosure supplied is qualitative only.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company operates four manufacturing plants supplying Hero MotoCorp, and during FY 2025-26 it invested in its Sanand facility, which management states will drive higher revenue from Tata Motors going forward; no rupee quantum, commissioning date or capacity number is given for that investment in the routed text. Customer footprint was widened from two to four OEM relationships, including a long-term supply contract with Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India and deeper engagement with Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, and the stated longer-term intent is to build a diversified engineering business spanning Automotive, Electronics, Aerospace and Defense. At the 68%-held material subsidiary Indutch Composites Technology Private Limited (Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat), mould manufacturing capacity was expanded during the year and about 20% revenue growth is expected next year. The Company also states it has not imported technology, so it has no information to offer on technology absorption. No installed-capacity table and no dated project/commissioning schedule appears anywhere in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- FY26 described as a structural, not merely cyclical, recovery in Indian consumption; private consumption growth rose to 10.5% in 2025 (from 8% in 2022-24), aided by tax relief, GST cuts, easing inflation and lower rates.
- Full-year private final consumption expenditure grew 7.7%, with retail inflation averaging just 2.5% over the first ten months of 2025 versus 4.9% a year earlier, boosting purchasing power.
- FY26 saw record industry-wide auto sales - passenger vehicles up 8% to 4.64 million units and two-wheelers up 10.7% to 21.71 million units - the first industry-wide record since FY19.
- Two-wheelers, closest to MAIL's core business, led the upturn with retail sales up 13.4% for the year and double-digit growth sustained through January-March 2026, which management reads as confirming a structural demand shift.
- Premiumisation: premium motorcycles grew 40.7% and scooters 18.5%.
- On the passenger vehicle side, mid-size and entry segments gained share - stated as directly supporting demand for MAIL's structural and chassis components.
- Consumer spending is projected to reach Rs 31,153 billion by 2027 and Rs 33,178 billion by 2028, described as giving Munjal Auto a durable tailwind for both existing volumes and new business across vehicle categories.
- Growth attributed to new business initiatives that are expected to continue contributing to growth.
- The Sanand facility investment made during FY26 is stated to drive higher revenue from Tata Motors going forward.
- Subsidiary Indutch Composites cited as executing strongly in the wind energy and advanced composites segments, having expanded mould manufacturing capacity and expecting about 20% revenue growth next year.
- Operating environment shaped by geopolitical developments, trade policy shifts, inflation, commodity price volatility, supply chain disruptions, forex fluctuations, and evolving regulations and customer preferences.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
